transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
- Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Louise Kievone.
President Trump is spending the final days
of the midterms imploring Republicans to vote in key races.
That includes in-person events in Iowa and Kansas.
NPR's Stephen Fowler reports from a rally in Dubuque.
- At his penultimate in-person event,
Trump did what Trump normally does.
Speak at length about many topics
from touting his accomplishments in office
to attacking Democrats and defended high gas prices
caused by the ongoing war in Iran.
- To be honest, I thought it would go up much higher
than it went up.
And, you know, I don't want to say because they'll say,
oh, he thinks it's, well, it's a very small price
to pay for the security of this country.
- Also in the nearly two-hour speech,
Trump commented on Republican U.S. Senate nominee
Ashley Henson's weight, heckled "protester,"
that's "stupid," and promises to send Americans money
if Republicans kept control of Congress,
something he cannot do.
Stephen Fowler, NPR News, Dubuque, Iowa.
- A federal judge has thrown out
the Trump administration's lawsuit
over the U.S. Senate race in Alaska.
NPR's Hansi Lo Wang reports the administration will appeal.
- The Trump administration asked the judge
to block the certification of results
from the U.S. Senate race in Alaska
if the Republican incumbent loses.
But U.S. District Judge Saren Gleason
found the administration does not have the ability
to bring this lawsuit.
President Trump said he ordered it to be filed
because out of the four Senate candidates
on Alaska's ballot, two have similar names,
the Republican incumbent, Senator Dan Sullivan,
and Daniel Sullivan Jr.,
who is not affiliated with a local party.
In June, the Alaska Supreme Court ruled
Daniel Sullivan Jr. has the right to run as a candidate.
A recent New York Times report
that NPR has not independently confirmed
says Democratic campaign operatives
were behind efforts to prop up Sullivan Jr.
as a spoiler candidate.
The Democratic candidate, Mary Peltola,
has denied any involvement.
Hansi Lo Wang, NPR News.
- Crypto exchange Binance says it has replaced
most of the cryptocurrencies that were stolen
from customer accounts and a massive cyber hack
earlier this week, and PR's Rafael Naum has details.
- The cryptocurrencies were lost by customers
after the exchange was hacked
by a North Korean military unit.
All in all, the hackers made off
with over $6 billion worth of cryptocurrencies.
Binance is using part of its own crypto holdings
or buying them in the markets
in order to be able to replace the stolen haul
suffered by its customers.
Traders turn to crypto exchanges such as Binance
to trade digital assets such as Bitcoin.
These investors also hold their cryptocurrencies
in accounts at the exchange itself,
making them a tempting target for hackers.
Rafael Naum, NPR News.
- 53-year-old Senator Chris Murphy
is reported to be making a smooth recovery
after having a stroke Saturday.
The Connecticut Democrat is not on the ballot this cycle.
This is NPR News in Washington.
At least six people were killed and dozens injured
in Halloween weekend shootings
in American nightlife districts.
Police in Dallas where the worst violence occurred
said four people are dead, 15 injured
following separate shootings.
Police in college towns like Fayetteville, Arkansas,
Birmingham, Alabama, Newark, Delaware
and Bloomington, Illinois also reported shootings.
Colorado's Governor Jared Polis submitted a formal request
for a disaster declaration from the White House
following extreme flooding in the state
from member station KSUT's Adam Burke has more.
- The formal request documents damage
from extreme flooding late last month,
which destroyed roads, buildings and critical infrastructure
along several watersheds in Southwest Colorado
and Northwest New Mexico.
Colorado's formal request estimates
that flooding recovery will cost $27 million
in Rio Grande County and Archuleta County.
Governor Polis stressed in social media posts
that reconstruction costs could be far higher
than estimated.
If approved by President Trump,
the Governor's request could unlock emergency relief funding
from the Federal Emergency Management Agency.
For NPR News, I'm Adam Burke in Durango.
- In the New York City Marathon today,
Andreas Aumgren of Sweden won the men's race
with a time of two hours, six minutes and one second.
He beat Yamuna Berhan-Krippa of Italy by 13 seconds.
Sheila Chepkarui, a 2024 champion from Kenya
won the women's race at two hours, 24 minutes and 36 seconds.
I'm Louise Schiavone, NPR News, Washington.
- This message comes from Integrative Therapeutics,
makers of Cortisol Manager,

topics.text: Trump campaigns in Iowa and Kansas, defends high gas prices from Iran war in Dubuque
Federal judge tosses Trump administration's lawsuit over Alaska Senate race; administration will appeal
Binance replaces most cryptocurrency stolen in hack attributed to North Korean military unit
Senator Chris Murphy recovering well after stroke Saturday, Connecticut Democrat not on ballot
Shootings over Halloween weekend in Dallas and several college towns leave at least six dead
Colorado Governor Jared Polis requests federal disaster declaration for late-October flooding in Southwest Colorado
Andreas Aumgren of Sweden wins men's New York City Marathon; Sheila Chepkarui of Kenya wins women's race
